name: Ford GT
hook: A supercharged tribute to the GT40 that beat Ferrari, built for Ford's centennial.

name: BMW M3 (E30)
hook: A homologation special that became the most successful touring car ever.

name: Lotus Carlton
hook: A 176 mph saloon that British MPs tried to have banned.

name: Porsche 911 Carrera RS 2.7
hook: The ducktail that Porsche thought nobody would buy sold out in a week.

name: Lotus Elise S1
hook: A glued aluminium chassis so light the whole car weighs less than a big engine.

name: Renault Clio V6
hook: A supermini with the back seats ripped out and a V6 bolted in their place.

name: Peugeot 205 GTI 1.9
hook: The hot hatch most often cited as the best of them all.

name: Porsche 718 Cayman GT4
hook: A manual, naturally aspirated flat-six in the middle, in the 2020s.

name: Alfa Romeo 4C
hook: A carbon tub car for the price of a hot hatch, with no power steering at all.

name: Ferrari F40
hook: The last car Enzo Ferrari signed off, with no carpet, no door handles, and 200 mph.

name: Jaguar XJ220
hook: Promised a V12 and four-wheel drive; delivered a twin-turbo V6 and a lawsuit.

name: McLaren F1
hook: Central driving seat, gold-lined engine bay, and a top speed record that stood for years.

name: Porsche Carrera GT
hook: A cancelled Le Mans V10 that ended up in a road car with a wooden gear knob.

name: Bugatti Veyron 16.4
hook: Ten radiators, four turbos, and a thousand horsepower, built to hit 407 km/h.

name: Ferrari F50
hook: A Formula 1 V12 bolted directly to the chassis as a stressed member.

name: Lamborghini Countach LP400
hook: The wedge that put a poster on every bedroom wall, named after a gasp in Piedmontese.

name: Ferrari 288 GTO
hook: Built for a rally category that was cancelled before it ever raced.

name: Koenigsegg One:1
hook: One horsepower per kilogram, hence the name.

name: Cizeta-Moroder V16T
hook: A transverse V16 supercar financed by the disco producer behind Donna Summer.

name: Audi Sport quattro S1 E2
hook: The winged Group B monster that later stormed Pikes Peak.

name: Lancia Delta S4
hook: Supercharged and turbocharged at the same time, and mid-engined under a family hatch shape.

name: Peugeot 205 T16 Evolution 2
hook: The car that won the last two Group B championships before the class was killed.

name: Lancia Delta HF Integrale
hook: Six consecutive world manufacturers' titles, a record that still stands.

name: Subaru Impreza 22B STI
hook: A road-going tribute to three straight world titles; 400 cars sold out in under an hour.

name: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution VI Tommi Mäkinen Edition
hook: Named after the man who won four drivers' titles in a row in it.

name: Lancia Stratos HF
hook: The first car designed from scratch to win rallies, with a Ferrari V6 behind the seats.

name: Toyota Corolla WRC
hook: Toyota's comeback car after a year-long ban for a hidden turbo restrictor trick.

name: MG Metro 6R4
hook: A shopping car with a bespoke V6 in the back; its engine later powered the Jaguar XJ220.

name: Ford RS200
hook: A purpose-built Group B car that arrived just as Group B ended.

name: Citroën Xsara WRC
hook: Sébastien Loeb's first three world titles came in this.

name: McLaren MP4/4
hook: Won 15 of 16 races in a season, with Senna and Prost at war inside the same garage.

name: Williams FW14B
hook: Active suspension so effective it was banned; Mansell clinched the title in August.

name: Ferrari F2004
hook: Schumacher won 13 races in it; some of its lap records stood for over a decade.

name: Tyrrell P34
hook: The six-wheeled Formula 1 car, and it actually won a Grand Prix.

name: Brabham BT46B
hook: The fan car: raced once, won, and was withdrawn before anyone could ban it.

name: Lotus 49
hook: First car to use the Cosworth DFV, the engine that then won 155 Grands Prix.

name: Lotus 79
hook: The first true ground-effect car; drivers said it was like being on rails.

name: Mercedes-AMG F1 W11
hook: Statistically the most dominant F1 car ever, with a steering wheel you could push and pull.

name: Red Bull RB6
hook: Adrian Newey's blown-diffuser masterpiece and Vettel's first title.

name: Lotus 72
hook: Side radiators and a wedge nose; it won titles five years apart.

name: Audi R8 LMS
hook: The customer racer that turned GT3 into a global boom.

name: Porsche 911 GT3 R (991)
hook: A 4.0-litre flat-six racer sold to customers by the hundreds.

name: Mercedes-AMG GT3 Evo
hook: A 6.3-litre naturally aspirated V8 in an era of turbos.

name: Lamborghini Huracán GT3 Evo
hook: Won the Daytona 24 Hours three years running.

name: Nissan GT-R Nismo GT3
hook: A road-car-based front-engined GT3 that won the Bathurst 12 Hour.

name: McLaren 720S GT3
hook: A carbon-tub GT3 car that shares its chassis with the road car.

name: Bentley Continental GT3
hook: A two-tonne luxury coupe put on a diet and sent racing.

name: BMW M4 GT3
hook: Replaced a V8 with a turbo straight-six and a famously long, low body.

name: Porsche 911 GT1
hook: A Le Mans prototype with 911 headlights; the road version exists only because the rules demanded it.

name: Porsche 917K
hook: Porsche's first overall Le Mans win, and the star of Steve McQueen's film.

name: Ford GT40 Mk II
hook: Henry Ford II's revenge on Ferrari: a 1-2-3 finish at Le Mans.

name: Jaguar XJR-9
hook: A 7-litre V12 that broke Porsche's seven-year Le Mans streak.

name: Sauber-Mercedes C9
hook: Clocked 400 km/h on the Mulsanne, which got chicanes added the next year.

name: BMW V12 LMR
hook: BMW's only overall Le Mans win, in a car with a Williams-built chassis.

name: Audi R10 TDI
hook: The first diesel to win Le Mans, and it was almost silent.

name: Porsche 919 Hybrid
hook: A 2-litre V4 plus two hybrid systems; the Evo version later smashed the Nürburgring record.

name: Jaguar D-Type
hook: Aircraft-style monocoque and a tail fin, and three Le Mans wins in a row.

name: Toyota GT-One
hook: A road-legal loophole car whose fuel tank counted as the luggage compartment.

name: Ferrari 499P
hook: Ferrari returned to the top class after 50 years and won on the first try.

name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR
hook: Won the Mille Miglia at record pace, then was withdrawn from racing after the Le Mans disaster.

name: Nissan Skyline GT-R V-Spec (R34)
hook: Godzilla's last stand, with an in-dash telemetry screen years before anyone else.

name: Honda NSX-R
hook: The aluminium supercar Senna helped tune, stripped of 120 kg.

name: Mazda RX-7 (FD)
hook: Sequential twin turbos on a rotary, in one of the prettiest shapes of the decade.

name: Toyota Supra RZ (A80)
hook: The 2JZ engine that tuners pushed to four figures without opening the block.

name: Toyota Sprinter Trueno AE86
hook: A cheap rear-drive coupe that became the folk hero of Japanese mountain roads.

name: Lexus LFA
hook: A V10 that revved so fast the tachometer had to be digital.

name: Datsun 240Z
hook: The sports car that made America take Japanese cars seriously.

name: Toyota 2000GT
hook: Japan's first supercar, and a Bond car with the roof cut off to fit Sean Connery.

name: Honda Beat
hook: A mid-engined roadster with 656 cc and a 8,500 rpm redline, the last car Soichiro Honda approved.

name: Honda S2000
hook: 120 horsepower per litre from a naturally aspirated four, redlining at 9,000.

name: Nissan Silvia (S13)
hook: The affordable rear-drive coupe that built drifting.

name: Dodge Charger Daytona
hook: A nose cone and a wing taller than the roof, all to win NASCAR.

name: Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda
hook: 426 Hemi, shaker hood; convertibles now sell for millions.

name: Chevrolet Camaro ZL1
hook: An all-aluminium 427 ordered through a loophole; 69 were built.

name: Pontiac GTO
hook: The option package that started the muscle car era.

name: Ford Mustang GT 390 Fastback
hook: The Highland Green Bullitt car, found in a garage after decades.

name: Buick GNX
hook: A turbo V6 Buick that out-dragged Ferraris and Corvettes.

name: Dodge Challenger SRT Demon
hook: The first production car to lift its front wheels off the line.

name: Shelby Cobra 427
hook: A tiny British roadster with a 7-litre Ford V8 stuffed in.

name: Porsche 959 Paris-Dakar
hook: A twin-turbo supercar that won the Dakar Rally across the Sahara.

name: Ford F-150 Raptor
hook: A pickup with race-truck suspension travel from the showroom floor.

name: Mitsubishi Pajero Evolution
hook: A Dakar homologation special with a 3.5 V6 and wild wheel arches.

name: Meyers Manx
hook: The original fibreglass beach buggy that won the first Baja race.

name: Lamborghini LM002
hook: A Countach V12 in a military truck, nicknamed the Rambo Lambo.

name: Toyota Land Cruiser FJ60
hook: The 4x4 that outlasts everything, from the outback to the Andes.

name: Peugeot 2008 DKR
hook: Two-wheel drive, huge tyres, and a Dakar win against 4x4s.

name: Range Rover Classic
hook: Displayed in the Louvre as a work of industrial design.

name: Bugatti Type 57SC Atlantic
hook: Riveted dorsal seam because the alloy body could not be welded; four were built.

name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing
hook: The doors open upward because the racing chassis was too tall for normal ones.

name: Jaguar E-Type
hook: Enzo Ferrari reportedly called it the most beautiful car ever made.

name: Ferrari 250 GTO
hook: Thirty-six built; now the most expensive car ever sold.

name: Tucker 48
hook: A third headlight that turned with the wheel, and a company crushed after 51 cars.

name: Citroën DS
hook: Hydropneumatic suspension so good it saved a president from an assassination attempt.

name: Austin Mini
hook: A transverse engine and wheels at the corners; it changed how small cars are packaged.

name: Lamborghini Miura
hook: The first mid-engined supercar, with a transverse V12 sitting sideways.

name: Aston Martin DB5
hook: The Bond car, with an ejector seat only in the film.

name: Bentley 4½ Litre Blower
hook: A supercharged racer W.O. Bentley himself hated.

name: Alfa Romeo 155 V6 TI
hook: An Italian saloon that stormed the German championship in its first year.

name: BMW M3 Sport Evolution (E30 DTM)
hook: The road car exists to make this racer legal.

name: Volvo 850 Estate BTCC
hook: A station wagon in a touring car championship, with a dog in the back for the photos.

name: Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16 Evolution II
hook: A boxy saloon with a wing designed in a wind tunnel, sold in just 502 copies.

name: Opel Calibra V6 DTM
hook: Four-wheel drive and a screaming V6 in the wildest touring car era.

name: Nissan Primera BTCC
hook: A family car that won the British championship outright.

name: Ford Sierra RS500 Cosworth
hook: Five hundred road cars built so the race version could run a bigger turbo.

name: Holden Commodore VE V8 Supercar
hook: Five-litre V8s and Bathurst, the race that stops a nation.

name: Mini Cooper S (racing)
hook: A tiny car that beat big saloons on tight circuits and won Monte Carlo three times.

name: Lancia Stratos Zero
hook: Under a metre tall; you climb in through the windscreen.

name: Phantom Corsair
hook: A six-seat teardrop with no door handles, built by a ketchup heir.

name: Lincoln Futura
hook: A double-bubble show car that became the 1966 Batmobile.

name: GM Firebird I
hook: A gas-turbine jet fighter with wheels, and it was road tested.

name: Mercedes-Benz C111
hook: Rotary-engined, gullwinged, orange, and never sold despite blank cheques.

name: Jaguar C-X75
hook: Micro gas turbines feeding electric motors; it later starred as a Bond villain's car.

name: Ferrari 512 S Modulo
hook: A flying saucer on a Le Mans chassis; finally made to run in 2018.

name: Aston Martin Bulldog
hook: A wedge built to hit 200 mph; it finally did, 43 years later.

name: Cadillac Sixteen
hook: A 13.6-litre V16 with a thousand horsepower, in a luxury sedan.

name: Cadillac Cyclone
hook: Radar in the nose cones and a bubble canopy, in 1959.
